correctness.rationale: If j is the highest index of an irrational nonconstant coefficient, the coefficient of degree j in f(Dm+u)/D is that coefficient times D^{j−1} plus a rational. Weyl therefore applies separately in every n-residue class. The half-open floor-residue intervals are correct also for negative floors. Exactly min(p,k) pairs fail at p, out of p². Theorem 1.3 of Holdridge has the required degree and irrationality hypotheses and bounds the large-common-prime exceptional set separately for every f+j; the finite union bound justifies taking the prime cutoff to infinity for each fixed k. Inclusion-exclusion at offsets −1 and r then gives the stated second difference, with shifted blocks covered by replacing f by f−1. Positivity follows by specifying two distinct primes greater than r+1, one per endpoint and neither conflicting with the interior, and sieving the interior at the other primes using the same tail bound. For the asymptotics, the tail in C_r has log O(r∑_{p>r}p^{−2})=o(1); Mertens gives its main term. In Q_r=C_{r+1}/C_r, the sum of (p²−r)^{−1} differs from ∑_{p>r}p^{−2} by O(r∑p^{−4})=O(r^{−2}), so PNT gives 1−Q_r∼1/(r log r). In δ_r/C_r=(1−Q_r)²+Q_r(Q_{r+1}−Q_r), changes of the common factors are O(∑p^{−4})=O(r^{−3}). With composite r+1 this is negligible against the square; with prime r+1=p the disappearing factor gives a positive ∼p^{−2} term that dominates the square. Both constants and the stated order of the limits follow. Finite CRT reproduction at moduli 30 and 210 confirms only the finite counting step.

value.rationale: This is a complete positive distribution of exact run lengths for a natural coprimality predicate; the effect is not just an Euler-product rewrite.
